question: Should OpenClaw core accept a generic durable allow-always plugin approval API now, or should this PR be narrowed until the durable trust, revocation, and built-in Skill Workshop scope model are explicitly settled?
rationale: The PR adds a plugin-facing API and persistent approval state that can suppress future prompts for sensitive actions; source review found mechanical bugs, but maintainers still need to accept the long-lived security/compatibility contract before it ships.

options.title: Repair and keep the generic API
options.body: Land the core API only after the Skill Workshop owner/scope, docs, tests, and rebase are fixed and durable trust semantics are explicitly accepted.

options.title: Split Skill Workshop opt-in out
options.body: Land only the generic persistence mechanism after API review and keep Skill Workshop on allow-once/deny until its owner/audit model is ready.

options.title: Pause this direction
options.body: Keep durable allow-always persistence plugin-owned or feature-specific until revocation and trust boundaries have a clearer product design.

recommendation.title: Repair and keep the generic API
recommendation.body: Land the core API only after the Skill Workshop owner/scope, docs, tests, and rebase are fixed and durable trust semantics are explicitly accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is tied to Skill Workshop lifecycle approval ownership, which shakkernerd introduced and recently refactored.
